data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Nessi was the goddess of the forest, associated with fertility and protection. She was often depicted as a snake or a woman with the upper body of a snake. The name Nessi carries the meaning “Goddess of the Forest” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nessi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the forest and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nessi belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Forest.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nessi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nessi may evoke associations with the Greek goddess Nessus, particularly her connection to the forest and natural beauty.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, Nessi may symbolize a deep connection to nature and the divine feminine, embodying qualities of protection, fertility, and transformation. As Nessus was also associated with the underworld and redemption in some mythologies, this name could also carry a deeper spiritual significance, representing a journey towards healing, purification, and rebirth.
